title: Ops Quicksteps: Embedded Runlet Kit
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Oncall engineers continuously run short, idempotent remediation steps (kill pod, rotate key, restart worker, toggle feature flag). Today these actions live as scattered shell snippets, ad-hoc admin scripts, or as large playbooks that require operator intervention. We want a lightweight, embeddable primitive — a "runlet" — that can be registered in the Console, surfaced in the CLI, and executed from runbooks-as-tasks. Runlets should be small, parameterized, idempotent, and carry automated safety checks (RBAC, audit context, dry-run).

Goal: Deliver an "embedded runlet kit" that developers/engineers can author as YAML or small TypeScript modules, register to the Admin Catalog, and invoke from: (a) Redwood Console quick-actions, (b) redwood-ops CLI, and (c) runbook taskgraphs. Kit must integrate with existing audit logs, support KMS-sourced secrets at invocation-time, and emit structured telemetry for cost/latency/side-effects.

Non-goals: Not replacing full runbook orchestration or external incident automation engines. This is intentionally narrow: 1-3 step primitives with conservative safety rails.

Acceptance criteria:
- Authoring: a clear, documented format (YAML + optional TypeScript hook) and linter. Example runlet for "drain node" plus test harness in repo.
- Registration: POST /admin/runlets API + Console UI that lists runlets with schema-driven form generation for parameters.
- Execution: CLI and Console can execute runlets in foreground with streaming logs; support --dry-run and --assume-role flags.
- Safety: RBAC check at invocation, audit entry written with invocation metadata, and automatic confirmation for destructive primitives.
- Observability: Each runlet invocation emits structured events (trace id, duration, side-effects) to existing ops telemetry pipeline.
- Replays: Runlets can be recorded as a step in runbook tasks and replayed safely in staging via a recorded-params toggle.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Authoring surface: YAML-first lowers bar for SREs; TypeScript hooks allow complex logic. We will support both but prioritize YAML for v1.
- Execution model: runlets run as short-lived containers inside an isolated runner service vs. invoking arbitrary customer infra commands. Containers give better auditing and sandboxing; serverless runner uses existing Helix infra.
- Secrets handling: prefer ephemeral KMS-wrapped secrets delivered at runtime rather than inlined credentials. This requires a KMS path to be specified in the runlet manifest.
- Safety vs speed: mandatory RBAC check on server reduces speed by ~100ms but necessary for security. Provide a cached token for repeated safe operations within a single invocation session.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec: draft YAML schema + example runlets (drain-node, restart-worker, rotate-api-key).
2) Runner: lightweight service + container image builder, reuse existing opslet runtime.
3) API + registry: admin-runlets service with REST endpoints and soft-delete.
4) Console: Quick-actions panel + auto-generated param forms.
5) CLI: redwood-ops integration with streaming logs and --dry-run.
6) Telemetry: add trace/span + structured event schema, link to Cost/Latency dashboards.
7) Security review + audit logging: KMS & RBAC integration, HSM path for enterprise customers.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal opt-in group (SRE + Platform) for manual testing.
- Beta: enable on dev/staging projects with guardrails.
- GA: broad rollout with migration guide for existing scripts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Dangerous runlets: enforce explicit destructive flag, require two-step confirmation for delete-like actions.
- Secrets leakage: require KMS reference; reject inline secret fields at linter stage.
- Non-idempotent hooks: provide test harness that runs runlets against a sandbox environment; require idempotency check annotations.

Telemetry KPIs:
- Average runlet execution time
- Number of runlet invocations per week
- % of invocations with dry-run vs actual
- Incidents mitigated via runlet within 15m
